skill.name: example-skill
skill.description: A prompt-only example skill that demonstrates a minimal skill structure and helps authors understand, create, and debug skills.
skill.summary: Use a minimal example to understand, create, and troubleshoot AI skills.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only SKILL.md file. Manual semantic review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable code, or business-logic abuse. The skill appears safe as a minimal documentation and guidance example.

content.user_title: Build Example Skills From a Simple Template
content.value_statement: New skill authors need a clear starting point for structure and workflow. This skill explains a minimal skill template and guides creation, testing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains the basic structure of a minimal skill file.
Guides users through understanding, creating, and debugging skills.
Encourages starting with a minimum viable skill.
Promotes early testing after each skill change.
Frames iteration as part of normal skill improvement.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, tools, or automation.
Does not provide advanced marketplace packaging guidance.
Does not validate skill files or run security checks.
Does not include domain-specific templates beyond a minimal example.

use_cases.title: Learn Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Review a compact example before writing a first prompt-only skill.

use_cases.title: Plan a Minimal Skill
use_cases.description: Define a small starting scope before adding references, tools, or workflows.
use_cases.target_user: Developer building an AI assistant workflow

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Skill Drafts
use_cases.description: Use the intake flow to focus debugging on structure, instructions, or expected behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this example skill is structured and what each section is meant to do.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Minimal Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn this idea into a minimal skill. Keep the scope small and identify the first test I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Debug My Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my skill draft for unclear instructions, missing intake steps, and places where testing should happen earlier.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Through Iteration
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my current skill behavior with the intended workflow and suggest focused improvements for the next version.

output_examples.input: Explain the parts of this example skill.
output: The front matter names the skill and describes when to use it.
The principles section gives simple guidance for building skills.
The intake section asks the user to choose the help they need.

output_examples.input: Help me start a new skill for release notes.
output_examples.output: Start with a short description, one focused workflow, and a simple intake question. Test the skill with one real release note request before adding more behavior.

output_examples.input: My skill gives broad answers instead of specific help.
output_examples.output: Narrow the intake choices, state the expected task more directly, and add one test prompt for each supported workflow.

best_practices: Start with the smallest useful workflow before adding extra sections.
Test after each meaningful change to catch unclear behavior early.
Revise instructions based on real usage and repeated failures.
anti_patterns: Adding complex workflows before the core skill behavior is tested.
Using vague intake questions that do not guide the assistant.
Treating the example as a complete production packaging guide.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users understand a minimal skill structure and start creating or debugging simple skills.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or install tools?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only skill with guidance text and no executable automation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on simple principles, a small starting scope, and early testing.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready skills by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a minimal example, not full packaging, validation, or release guidance.

faq.question: How should I use it while drafting?
faq.answer: Ask for structure help first, create a small draft, test it, and then iterate on observed issues.
